title: Switch Equipment Procurement
text: After that, I went out to hunt some monsters to level up Kou a bit. My father seemed to be enjoying himself fighting in a temporary party with a mercenary from Siltvelt. That panda Beastman seemed like a really caring guy. When I got back from hunting, my father was having a good time with him at the tavern.
“Well, I’ve got some business to attend to…”
“Oh! Let’s go hunting again sometime when we meet up.”
“Yeah. That was a worthwhile time.”
“I had a decent time too.”
“Lars-chan! That was fun! Next time, teach me how to be cool, okay?”
“Bye-bye.”

My father-in-law and the others said goodbye to the panda beastman and came over to me. To be able to build friendly relationships with others in the blink of an eye—that’s my Father for you. …Thanks to him, I’ve even been taken under his wing, so I owe him a huge debt of gratitude.
“Well, let’s go.”
“Understood.”
Avoiding prying eyes, I used a portal to meet up with the carriage as planned.
“What were you doing, Motoyasu-kun?”
“I was planting and examining the ‘Bio-Plants’—the plant seeds that my future Father would likely have used—in Siltvelt.”
“Ah, come to think of it, you did mention something like that.”
“Oink…”
That Lazy Pig is looking this way and grunting. To interrupt a precious conversation between me and my Father like that… I really should just eliminate it from this world…
“Huh? Couldn’t you have conducted the experiment on Elena’s family estate?　“Well, I suppose so, but if something we gave them went haywire, wouldn’t that put us in a bad spot?”
That’s true. If the seeds we gave them caused any trouble, my Father would be framed as the culprit, giving the Melromarc lot a pretext for action. I can’t let that happen.
“Oink oink.”
The Lazy Pig seems to be nodding in agreement with Father’s words.
“Huh? If it works out, wouldn’t that be a good thing in the end? Well, I guess… if they secure a spot for us, it might be a good way to make some money down the road.”
“Spear Guy! You understand what I’m saying, right?”
“I do.”
“Keel. You’re looking even more delicious. Kou, I’m drooling.”
“I’m not food!”
Keel barks “Woof, woof” and growls at Kou.
“No, Kou. Sakura’s here to protect Keel-kun.”

Sakura-chan answers as she hugs Keel tightly from behind. Among the Filolial-sama, Sakura-chan has become the Big Sister, hasn’t she? That position was originally supposed to be Yuki-chan’s, but perhaps it’s a matter of personality?
“Using the letter of introduction I used for my Class Up, I managed to get the people of Siltvelt to provide us with a farm we can manage.”

That’s quite convenient. My father could go himself, of course, but he’s operating undercover. Considering what happened last time, the people of Siltvelt might end up giving him a grand welcome… or so it seems. Better safe than sorry, I suppose.

Well, for that reason, I’ll have to go check on things whenever I have a chance from now on. Ideally, I’d like to secure enough to use as weapon materials. After all, a single seed is only enough to unlock a weapon. It would be best to keep investigating what kind of changes occur.
“So, Motoyasu, did you find out anything?”
“It grew rapidly for a while after planting. What happens after that is still unclear.”
“Huh… If it goes well, maybe we can make some money selling it as peddlers…?”
“That’s right. That’s the whole point of this experiment.”

I seem to recall hearing in the future world that securing food had become a major issue due to the effects of the waves. For that reason, I believe the food that Father possessed was a groundbreaking product that played a role in resolving the food crisis.

Currently, for one reason or another, the whole world is grappling with food shortages. For now, we’re managing with just rising prices, but back in the original world, when Father first began developing the village, the food situation had already taken a turn for the worse. Well, thanks to the plants that grew on my Father’s estate, it seems Melromarc managed to resolve the issue to some extent.

If that plant is the one I’ve obtained… it’ll truly be a money tree. We could sell it at a reasonable price, or we could distribute it to build goodwill—either way, it’ll boost Father’s reputation. Right now, gaining the people’s trust is the top priority. I deduce that my future father gained that trust in this way.
“Well then, let’s get the people of Siltvelt to help us with the research. Should I lend a hand?”
“It’ll be fine. Father, please just accept the results I present to you.”
“Even so… personally, I’m curious about those seeds.”
“Well, it’s just a matter of observing them periodically. It might be a good idea to stop by on our way out of Siltvelt.”
“Well, I suppose I’ll do that, then?”
“The problem is, once your identity is revealed, you might be invited to Siltvelt Castle.”
“…Apparently, they’ll listen to me for the time being, but back in the future, I heard you were set up on marriage proposals day after day and even poisoned by Sakura-chan and the others, right?”

That’s the issue my future father-in-law is concerned about. Last time, my father was furious that Sakura and the others had been poisoned. When I brought up that story again this time, he looked displeased, so it seems he doesn’t fully trust the people of Siltvelt. That’s why he’s reluctant to go to the castle.
“There are only a few days left until the wave hits… I’d at least like to prove my innocence and avert the danger of war before that happens.”
“You’re right.”
“As for what happens after I defeat that guy Takt… I wonder how I can prevent a war…”
That’s the problem. Since I can barely tell pigs apart, there are only a handful of ways I can deal with the war that would break out after defeating Takt.

One option is to kill all the witnesses. When Takt sets a trap for me, if I go ahead alone, take him down, and then slaughter everyone around him, I might be able to prevent him from escaping to his country and thus avoid a war.

Another option is to let history unfold as it did in the first world: let him attempt world conquest, defeat him, and then have him executed by each nation. There are probably other ways, but I haven’t had the chance to try them.

In that sense, you could say that simply staying in Siltvelt is like leaving a spark that could ignite a new war. However… I’m torn about whether I should expose the fact that the “Claw Hero” is an imposter. Either way, it’d be best to avoid meeting him if at all possible.

As much as possible, I’ll make use of the land in Siltvelt without going near the castle. I believe the higher-ups in Siltvelt understand that my Father is occasionally in the country. They’ll likely turn a blind eye to this, seeing it as part of a strategy to undermine our arch-rival, Melromarc, from within.
“For now, I suppose we just need to keep training so we’re ready when the time comes.”
“That’s right!”
And so, that day came to an end.

Three days until we reach the coast. We’ve arrived at the town below Melromarc Castle. Our goal this time is to procure equipment. Using the money we earned from peddling as capital, we stopped by the weapons shop. The Lazy Pig, looking annoyed, is keeping watch in the carriage with Kou.
“Hey! Isn’t that An-chan? How’s it going?”
“So-so, I guess. I’ve been wanting some new gear for a while now.”
“Hey, old man! I finally got recognized by the Spear Guy!”
With that, Keel—in the form of a puppy—started making a scene. The old man at the weapon shop looked at Keel and spoke up.
“Oh? That voice… isn’t that Keel, the slave An-chan bought? Looks like he’s successfully become a Beastman.”
“How about that! Cool, huh?”
“If anything, you’re more like a pet monster.”
“Even you’re saying that, Father!? Am I not cool?! I am!”
Father patted and picked up Keel, who was slumping dejectedly. He’s totally a puppy.
“Don’t treat me like a kid, bro!”
“Yeah, yeah. Keel-kun is cool.”
“Ugh…”
“Haha, I’m glad you’re having fun. So? What brings you here?”
“It’s obvious why I’d come to a weapons shop, isn’t it?”
“True. You want weapons and armor, right? What’s your budget, and what are you looking for? I can even take trade-ins if you want.”
“Well then… maybe I’ll sell you some of the weapons I took from the bandits who attacked me when I first started peddling.”
“If you’ve got any materials on hand, I can make you a custom order, too.”
“Oh, you handle that kind of thing too?”
“You look like you’d love that, An-chan. Sounds like fun.”
My father replies with a slightly exasperated laugh.
“Yeah. It’s great, isn’t it? Custom-made gear instead of off-the-shelf stuff. Plus, having gear made from materials I gathered myself—doesn’t that make you feel more attached to it?”
“I can’t say I don’t get where you’re coming from.”
“That said… the materials I’ve gathered in between my traveling sales trips might not be quite up to par…”
With that, Father shows the old man the bag full of materials he’s collected.
“Hmm… with these, I could probably make all sorts of things. It’ll definitely turn out better than the gear you’re wearing now, right?”
“So, could you make that for us?”
“Sure thing. Though it depends on whether you want weapons or armor.”
“It’d be a good idea to beef up Keel and Sakura’s gear, too.”
“Hmm?”
“I want a sharper weapon! Shilt—”
“Keel, shut your mouth.”
Father covered Keel’s mouth. That’s right. You see, the weapons we let them use in Siltvelt are intentionally blocked in Melromarc.

We’ve been letting them use weapons that my Father and I found as drops. Since they have high Attack Power, I can’t say I don’t understand why they’d want to use them here too. But if we were to reveal that here, the country might send assassins or start some weird feud with us.
“I’m not exactly clueless about what you’re trying to say.”
“Sorry.”
“It’s fine. For now, should we start with Keel-kun and the young lady’s weapons?”
“I suppose so… but Kou and Yuki-chan don’t need equipment, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Yuki-chan and Kou’s combat styles are geared toward fighting monsters. We’ll have the monster merchants prepare their gear.”
“So, should we go later?”

Hmm… As things stand, neither Yuki-chan nor Kou are in any immediate need of equipment. Claws would be nice to have, but right now we should prioritize gathering gear for my Father and the others. Worst-case scenario, there might even be a claw dropped from a spear.
“You don’t need to worry about it.”
“Really?”
“It’s absolutely no problem at all.”

As things stand, there’s absolutely no need for Yuki-chan and the others to have claws. If we ever go somewhere where weapons are necessary, I’ll take care of it myself. Besides, we’ll avoid dangerous areas within Melromarc as much as possible, so it’ll be fine to wait until we have some extra money. So, for now, there’s no need for Yuki-chan and the others to get equipment. Since Filolial-sama fights using her own claws and beak, she doesn’t need weapons nearly as much as humans do.
